This page describes quotas and request limits for Cloud Storage. You can request increases to quotas, but limits cannot be adjusted.

Quotas and limits are subject to change.

Buckets

Limit Value Notes
Maximum bucket name size 63 characters

If the name contains a dot (.), the limit is 222 characters.
Maximum bucket creation and deletion rate per project Approximately one request every two seconds

Plan on fewer buckets and more objects in most cases. For example, a common design choice is to use one bucket per user of your project. However, if you're designing a system that adds many users per second, then design for many users in one bucket (with appropriate permissions) so that the bucket creation rate limit doesn't become a bottleneck.

Highly available applications shouldn't depend on bucket creation, deletion, or list operations in the critical path of their application. Bucket names are part of a centralized and global namespace: any dependency on this namespace creates a single point of failure for your application. If a location is temporarily unavailable, the bucket list operation might return only a partial list of buckets. Due to these considerations and the bucket creation/deletion limit, the recommended practice for highly available services on Cloud Storage is to pre-create all the buckets necessary.

Maximum bytes of data that can be stored across all the zonal buckets per project, per zone

This limit only applies to buckets that use Rapid Bucket.

 1 TB default limit, but might be lower or higher based on your project's billing account history

For more information about zonal buckets, see Rapid Bucket.
Maximum bucket restoration rate per project Approximately one request every two seconds
Maximum rate of bucket metadata updates per bucket One update per second Rapid updates to a single bucket (for example, changing the CORS configuration) might result in throttling errors.
Maximum number of principals that can be granted IAM roles per bucket

1,500 principals for all IAM roles

100 principals for legacy IAM roles

 See Principal types for more information.
Maximum number of Pub/Sub notification configurations per bucket 100 notification configurations
Maximum number of concurrent bucket relocations supported from the same location within a project 5 buckets See Bucket relocation for more information.
Maximum number of Pub/Sub notification configurations set to trigger for a specific event 10 notification configurations
Maximum number of custom attributes in a Pub/Sub notification configuration 10 custom attributes
Maximum retention period that can be set for Bucket Lock 3,155,760,000 seconds (100 years)
Maximum soft delete retention duration 90 days
Maximum number of prefixes and suffixes in total when using matchesPrefix and matchesSuffix lifecycle conditions across all rules on a bucket. 1,000 For information about Object Lifecycle Management, see Object Lifecycle Management.

Objects

Limit Value Notes
Maximum object size 5 TiB

This limit applies regardless of write method, including object composition, resumable uploads, and multipart uploading.
Maximum combined size of all custom metadata keys and values per object 8 KiB
Maximum object name size for objects in a flat namespace bucket 1024 bytes (UTF-8 encoded)
Maximum object name size for objects in a hierarchical namespace enabled bucket Folder name: 512 bytes (UTF-8 encoded)
base name: 512 bytes (UTF-8 encoded)
.
Maximum rate of writes to the same object name One write per second Writing to the same object name at a rate above the limit might result in throttling errors. For more information, see Object immutability.
Maximum rate of object metadata updates to a single object One update per second Updating object metadata at a rate above the limit might result in throttling errors.
Maximum rate of object writes in a bucket Unlimited Includes uploading, updating, and deleting objects. Buckets initially support roughly 1,000 writes per second and then scale as needed.
Maximum rate of object reads in a bucket Unlimited Includes reading object data, reading object metadata, and listing objects. Buckets initially support roughly 5,000 object reads per second and then scale as needed. However, note that there are bandwidth limits.
Maximum number of access control list entries (ACLs) 100 ACLs per object For more information, see ACL scopes.
Maximum number of source objects in an object composition 32 objects in a single compose request
Maximum number of components that make up a composite object Unlimited While there is no limit to the number of components that make up a composite object, the componentCount metadata associated with a composite object saturates at 2,147,483,647, and the final composite object must adhere to the 5 TiB size limit that applies to all objects in Cloud Storage.
Maximum retention time that can be set for Object Retention Lock 3,155,760,000 seconds (100 years) from the current date and time
Maximum initial queries per second (QPS) limits for reading and writing objects in buckets with hierarchical namespace enabled Up to 8 times higher QPS compared to buckets without hierarchical namespace enabled For information about optimizing performance when working with folders, see Folder management.
Maximum contexts per object 50
Maximum combined size of all object context keys and values per object 25 KiB (UTF-8 encoded)
Maximum length of an object context key 256 bytes (UTF-8 encoded)
Maximum length of an object context value 256 bytes (UTF-8 encoded)

Rapid Cache

Limit Value Notes
Maximum Rapid Cache cache size 1 PiB

The cache size automatically scales up or down to the amount of data stored in the cache, up to a maximum of 1 PiB. The cache size is equal to the amount of data ingested into the cache minus the amount of data evicted. For example, if a workload ingests 100 GiB of data, the cache size will grow to 100 GiB. If 50 GiB of data is subsequently evicted, the cache size will reduce to 50 GiB.

Your cache size limit might be lower based on your project's billing account history. If resources are limited, cache creations can be halted or existing caches can stop growing and evict data on a least recently used (LRU) algorithm to make room for new data.

You can request an increase of cache storage beyond 1 PiB by contacting your Technical Account Manager or Google representative.
Maximum Rapid Cache data usage bandwidth limit per-project, per-zone 20 Tbps

The cache bandwidth limit automatically scales according to the amount of data stored in the cache at a rate of 20 Gbps per 1 TiB of data, with a base value of 100 Gbps.

You can increase the starting or total amount of cache bandwidth by increasing the amount of data stored in the cache or creating more caches in a zone. You can also request increasing the rate of bandwidth by contacting your Technical Account Manager or Google representative.

The cache bandwidth limit is separate from your project's maximum bandwidth quota. Reading data from the cache counts towards the cache bandwidth limit until the limit is reached, at which point data reads begin counting towards the project's bandwidth quota. Cache misses don't count towards the cache bandwidth limit.

Because the cache bandwidth limit applies on a per-project, per-zone basis, traffic from caches within the same project and zone count towards a common cache bandwidth limit, even if the caches are created for different buckets. For example, say Cache A is created in the zone us-east1-b for the bucket example-bucket-1, which is located in the project my-project. Cache B is created in us-east1-b for example-bucket-2, which is also located in my-project. Because Cache A and Cache B are both located in us-east1-b and my-project, traffic for both caches count towards the same cache bandwidth limit.

Note: Caches created for buckets in different location types don't count towards the same cache bandwidth limit, even if the caches are created in the same zone. For example, say both Cache A and Cache B are created in the us-east1-b zone, but Cache A belongs to a bucket in the us-east1 region and Cache B belongs to a bucket in the US multi-region. The caches would have separate cache bandwidth limits because their associated buckets have different location types, where one is stored in a region and the other is stored in a multi-region.
Maximum number of Rapid Cache caches being created concurrently per project, per zone 20 caches

The maximum number of caches that can be in the creating state at a given time.

Managed folders

Limit Value Notes
Maximum managed folder name size 1024 bytes (UTF-8 encoded)
Maximum number of managed folders in a Cloud Storage bucket Unlimited
Maximum managed folder nesting limit 15
Maximum rate of IAM policy updates per managed folder One update per second
Maximum number of principals that can be granted IAM roles per managed folder

1,500 principals for all IAM roles

 The number of principals granted an IAM role on a managed folder doesn't count towards the maximum number of principals that can be granted an IAM role on the bucket containing the managed folder, parent managed folders, or child managed folders.

JSON API requests

Limit Value Notes
Maximum total request payload of a batch request Less than 10 MiB Don't include more than 100 calls in a single request.
Maximum size of an object listing glob pattern 1024 bytes in UTF-8 encoding

XML API requests

Limit Value Notes
Maximum combined size of request URL and HTTP headers 16 KiB
Maximum number of buckets that can be returned when listing buckets 1,000 buckets The XML API returns buckets lexicographically by name.
Maximum number of parts in a multipart upload 10,000 parts The object assembled from these parts must adhere to the 5 TiB size limit that applies to all objects in Cloud Storage.
Maximum size of an individual part in a multipart upload 5 GiB
Minimum size of an individual part in a multipart upload 5 MiB There is no minimum size limit on the last part of a multipart upload. As a result, this limit is not enforced at the time a part is uploaded, but is instead enforced at the time you attempt to complete the upload.
Maximum length of time a multipart upload and its uploaded parts can remain unfinished or idle in a bucket Unlimited
Maximum number of different multipart uploads that can simultaneously occur for an object Unlimited
Maximum length of time to complete a resumable upload session 7 days The length of time is measured starting from the resumable upload being initiated.

HMAC keys for service accounts

There is a limit of at most 10 HMAC keys per service account. Deleted keys don't count towards this limit.

Inventory reports

There is a limit of at most 100 inventory report configurations per source bucket.

Storage batch operations jobs

This section describes current API restrictions and usage quotas on use of storage batch operations jobs.

Concurrent storage batch operations jobs

The following table describes the limit for concurrent in-progress jobs:

Maximum in-progress `jobs` Applies to
100 Per project per bucket's location

This table provides the metric, API methods, and default limits for each quota:

Metric API methods Default limits
storagebatchoperations.googleapis.com/create_requests storagebatchoperations.jobs.create 1200 requests/min/project
storagebatchoperations.googleapis.com/read_requests
  • storagebatchoperations.jobs.get
  • storagebatchoperations.jobs.list
 1200 requests/min/project

This section describes limits and quotas for Cloud Storage MCP server. For instructions on how to use it, see Use the Cloud Storage MCP server.

Limit Value
Maximum file size 8 MiB
Supported endpoints Global only

The following table describes rate limits per tool:

Quota Value

Requests for McpCreateBucket and McpWriteText 300/min/project/region

Bandwidth

Quota Value Notes

Maximum bandwidth for each zone that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services per project, per zone

Only available with Rapid Bucket.

 1 Tbps default quota per project, per zone, but might be lower or higher based on your project's billing account history

You can request quota increases by using the Google Cloud console on a per-project, per-zone basis. Alternatively, you can request quota increases by contacting your Technical Account Manager or Google representative.

To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see View and manage quotas.

To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see Bandwidth monitoring.

For more information about zonal buckets, see Rapid Bucket.
Maximum bandwidth for each region that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history

Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN is exempt from this quota.

You can request quota increases on a per-project basis.

To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see View and manage quotas.

To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see Bandwidth monitoring.
Maximum bandwidth for each dual-region that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services 200 Gbps default quota for each region within a dual-region for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history

Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN is exempt from this quota.

You can request a quota increase on a per-project basis.

To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see View and manage quotas.

To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see Bandwidth monitoring.
Maximum bandwidth for each multi-region that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history

Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN is exempt from this quota.

Each region within the given multi-region has a separate quota. For example, say the project my-project has a multi-region Google egress bandwidth quota of 200 Gbps for all regions within it. In this scenario, the us-east1 region has 200 Gbps of bandwidth when supporting data egress to Google services from buckets in the us multi-region, and the us-west1 region has 200 Gbps of bandwidth when supporting data egress to Google services from buckets in the us multi-region.

To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see View and manage quotas.

To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see Bandwidth monitoring.

You can request a quota increase on a per-project basis. Note that generally you should use buckets located in regions or dual-regions for workloads with high egress rates to Google services. For existing buckets in multi-regions that run large workloads in Google services, you can use Storage Transfer Service to move your data to a bucket in a region or dual-region.
Maximum egress bandwidth for Internet requests accessing data from buckets in a region 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history

Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN due to cache misses is included in this quota.

To learn how to view the Internet egress limits for a project, see View and manage quotas.

To learn how to view Internet egress usage for a project, see Bandwidth monitoring.

You can request quota increases on a per-project basis.
Maximum egress bandwidth for Internet requests accessing data from buckets in a dual-region 200 Gbps default quota for each region within a dual-region for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history

Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN due to cache misses is included in this quota.

To learn how to view the Internet egress limits for a project, see View and manage quotas.

To learn how to view Internet egress usage for a project by region, see Bandwidth monitoring.

You can request a quota increase on a per-project basis.
Maximum egress bandwidth for Internet requests accessing data from buckets in a given multi-region 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history

Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN due to cache misses is included in this quota.

Regions within the multi-region have separate multi-region Internet egress quotas. For example, say my-project sends data from a bucket located in the us multi-region to customers around the world. In this scenario, different regions within the us multi-region use their own Internet egress quota as data is sent from the bucket to different parts of the world. Typically, Internet egress quota is counted against the region that's geographically closest to the data's destination.

To learn how to view the Internet egress limits for a project, see View and manage quotas.

To learn how to view Internet egress usage for a project by region, see Bandwidth monitoring.

You can request a quota increase on a per-project basis.

When a project's bandwidth exceeds a certain quota, requests to affected buckets can be throttled or can be rejected with a retryable 429 - rateLimitExceeded error that includes details of the exceeded quota. See Bandwidth usage for information about monitoring your bandwidth.

# Quotas & limits Stay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences.



This page describes quotas and request limits for Cloud Storage. You
can request increases to quotas, but limits cannot be adjusted.

Quotas and limits are subject to change.

## Buckets

| Limit | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum [bucket name](/storage/docs/buckets#naming) size | 63 characters | If the name contains a dot (.), the limit is 222 characters. |
| Maximum bucket creation and deletion rate per project | Approximately one request every two seconds | Plan on fewer buckets and more objects in most cases. For example, a common design choice is to use one bucket per user of your project. However, if you're designing a system that adds many users per second, then design for many users in one bucket (with appropriate [permissions](/storage/docs/access-control/iam)) so that the bucket creation rate limit doesn't become a bottleneck.  Highly available applications shouldn't depend on bucket creation, deletion, or list operations in the critical path of their application. Bucket names are part of a centralized and global namespace: any dependency on this namespace creates a single point of failure for your application. If a location is temporarily unavailable, the bucket list operation might return only a partial list of buckets. Due to these considerations and the bucket creation/deletion limit, the recommended practice for highly available services on Cloud Storage is to pre-create all the buckets necessary. |
| Maximum bytes of data that can be stored across all the zonal buckets per project, per zone  This limit only applies to buckets that use [Rapid Bucket](/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-bucket). | 1 TB default limit, but might be lower or higher based on your project's billing account history | For more information about zonal buckets, see [Rapid Bucket](/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-bucket). |
| Maximum [bucket restoration](/storage/docs/use-soft-deleted-buckets) rate per project | Approximately one request every two seconds |  |
| Maximum rate of bucket metadata updates per bucket | One update per second | Rapid updates to a single bucket (for example, changing the CORS configuration) might result in throttling errors. |
| Maximum number of principals that can be granted IAM roles per bucket | 1,500 principals for all IAM roles  100 principals for [legacy IAM roles](/storage/docs/access-control/iam#acls) | See [Principal types](/storage/docs/access-control/iam#identities) for more information. |
| Maximum number of [Pub/Sub notification configurations](/storage/docs/pubsub-notifications) per bucket | 100 notification configurations |  |
| Maximum number of concurrent bucket relocations supported from the same location within a project | 5 buckets | See [Bucket relocation](/storage/docs/bucket-relocation/overview) for more information. |
| Maximum number of [Pub/Sub notification configurations](/storage/docs/pubsub-notifications#notification-configs) set to trigger for a specific event | 10 notification configurations |  |
| Maximum number of custom attributes in a [Pub/Sub notification configuration](/storage/docs/pubsub-notifications#notification-configs) | 10 custom attributes |  |
| Maximum retention period that can be set for [Bucket Lock](/storage/docs/bucket-lock) | 3,155,760,000 seconds (100 years) |  |
| Maximum [soft delete retention duration](/storage/docs/soft-delete#retention-duration) | 90 days |  |
| Maximum number of prefixes and suffixes in total when using [`matchesPrefix` and `matchesSuffix` lifecycle conditions](/storage/docs/lifecycle#matchesprefix-suffix) across all rules on a bucket. | 1,000 | For information about Object Lifecycle Management, see [Object Lifecycle Management](/storage/docs/lifecycle). |

## Objects

| Limit | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum [object](/storage/docs/objects) size | 5 TiB | This limit applies regardless of write method, including [object composition](/storage/docs/composite-objects), [resumable uploads](/storage/docs/resumable-uploads), and [multipart uploading](/storage/docs/multipart-uploads). |
| Maximum combined size of all [custom metadata](/storage/docs/metadata#custom-metadata) keys and values per object | 8 KiB |  |
| Maximum [object name](/storage/docs/objects#naming) size for objects in a flat namespace bucket | 1024 bytes (UTF-8 encoded) |  |
| Maximum [object name](/storage/docs/objects#naming) size for objects in a hierarchical namespace enabled bucket | **Folder name**: 512 bytes (UTF-8 encoded)  **base name**: 512 bytes (UTF-8 encoded) . |  |
| Maximum rate of writes to the same object name | One write per second | Writing to the same object name at a rate above the limit might result in throttling errors. For more information, see [Object immutability](/storage/docs/objects#immutability). |
| Maximum rate of object metadata updates to a single object | One update per second | Updating object metadata at a rate above the limit might result in throttling errors. |
| Maximum rate of object writes in a bucket | Unlimited | Includes uploading, updating, and deleting objects. Buckets initially support roughly 1,000 writes per second and then [scale as needed](/storage/docs/request-rate). |
| Maximum rate of object reads in a bucket | Unlimited | Includes reading object data, reading object metadata, and listing objects. Buckets initially support roughly 5,000 object reads per second and then [scale as needed](/storage/docs/request-rate). However, note that there are [bandwidth limits](/storage/quotas#bandwidth). |
| Maximum number of [access control list entries (ACLs)](/storage/docs/access-control/lists) | 100 ACLs per object | For more information, see [ACL scopes](/storage/docs/access-control/lists#scopes). |
| Maximum number of [source objects in an object composition](/storage/docs/composite-objects) | 32 objects in a single compose request |  |
| Maximum number of components that make up a [composite object](/storage/docs/composite-objects) | Unlimited | While there is no limit to the number of components that make up a composite object, the `componentCount` metadata associated with a composite object saturates at 2,147,483,647, and the final composite object must adhere to the 5 TiB size limit that applies to all objects in Cloud Storage. |
| Maximum retention time that can be set for [Object Retention Lock](/storage/docs/object-lock) | 3,155,760,000 seconds (100 years) from the current date and time |  |
| Maximum initial queries per second (QPS) limits for reading and writing objects in buckets with [hierarchical namespace enabled](/storage/docs/hns-overview) | Up to 8 times higher QPS compared to buckets without hierarchical namespace enabled | For information about optimizing performance when working with folders, see [Folder management.](/storage/docs/hns-buckets-best-practices#folder-management) |
| Maximum [contexts](/storage/docs/object-contexts) per object | 50 |  |
| Maximum combined size of all object context keys and values per object | 25 KiB (UTF-8 encoded) |  |
| Maximum length of an object context key | 256 bytes (UTF-8 encoded) |  |
| Maximum length of an object context value | 256 bytes (UTF-8 encoded) |  |

## Rapid Cache

| Limit | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum [Rapid Cache](/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-cache) cache size | 1 PiB | The cache size automatically scales up or down to the amount of data stored in the cache, up to a maximum of 1 PiB. The cache size is equal to the amount of data ingested into the cache minus the amount of data evicted. For example, if a workload ingests 100 GiB of data, the cache size will grow to 100 GiB. If 50 GiB of data is subsequently evicted, the cache size will reduce to 50 GiB.  Your cache size limit might be lower based on your project's billing account history. If resources are limited, cache creations can be halted or existing caches can stop growing and evict data on a least recently used (LRU) algorithm to make room for new data.  You can request an increase of cache storage beyond 1 PiB by contacting your Technical Account Manager or Google representative. |
| Maximum [Rapid Cache](/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-cache) data usage bandwidth limit per-project, per-zone | 20 Tbps | The cache bandwidth limit automatically scales according to the amount of data stored in the cache at a rate of 20 Gbps per 1 TiB of data, with a base value of 100 Gbps.  You can increase the starting or total amount of cache bandwidth by increasing the amount of data stored in the cache or creating more caches in a zone. You can also request increasing the rate of bandwidth by contacting your Technical Account Manager or Google representative.  The cache bandwidth limit is separate from your project's [maximum bandwidth quota](/storage/quotas#bandwidth). Reading data from the cache counts towards the cache bandwidth limit until the limit is reached, at which point data reads begin counting towards the project's bandwidth quota. Cache misses don't count towards the cache bandwidth limit.  Because the cache bandwidth limit applies on a per-project, per-zone basis, traffic from caches within the same project and zone count towards a common cache bandwidth limit, even if the caches are created for different buckets. For example, say Cache A is created in the zone `us-east1-b` for the bucket `example-bucket-1`, which is located in the project `my-project`. Cache B is created in `us-east1-b` for `example-bucket-2`, which is also located in `my-project`. Because Cache A and Cache B are both located in `us-east1-b` and `my-project`, traffic for both caches count towards the same cache bandwidth limit. |
| Maximum number of [Rapid Cache](/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-cache) caches being created concurrently per project, per zone | 20 caches | The maximum number of caches that can be in the `creating` state at a given time. |

## Managed folders

| Limit | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum [managed folder name](/storage/docs/managed-folders#managed_folder_names) size | 1024 bytes (UTF-8 encoded) |  |
| Maximum number of managed folders in a Cloud Storage bucket | Unlimited |  |
| Maximum [managed folder nesting limit](/storage/docs/managed-folders#managed_folder_names) | 15 |  |
| Maximum rate of [IAM policy](/storage/docs/managed-folders#managed-folder-iam) updates per managed folder | One update per second |  |
| Maximum number of principals that can be granted IAM roles per managed folder | 1,500 principals for all IAM roles | The number of principals granted an IAM role on a managed folder doesn't count towards the maximum number of principals that can be granted an IAM role on the bucket containing the managed folder, parent managed folders, or child managed folders. |

## JSON API requests

| Limit | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum total request payload of a [batch request](/storage/docs/batch) | Less than 10 MiB | Don't include more than 100 calls in a single request. |
| Maximum size of an object listing [glob pattern](/storage/docs/json_api/v1/objects/list#matchGlob) | 1024 bytes in UTF-8 encoding |  |

## XML API requests

| Limit | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum combined size of request URL and HTTP headers | 16 KiB |  |
| Maximum number of buckets that can be returned when listing buckets | 1,000 buckets | The XML API returns buckets lexicographically by name. |
| Maximum number of parts in a [multipart upload](/storage/docs/multipart-uploads) | 10,000 parts | The object assembled from these parts must adhere to the 5 TiB size limit that applies to all objects in Cloud Storage. |
| Maximum size of an individual part in a [multipart upload](/storage/docs/multipart-uploads) | 5 GiB |  |
| Minimum size of an individual part in a [multipart upload](/storage/docs/multipart-uploads) | 5 MiB | There is no minimum size limit on the last part of a multipart upload. As a result, this limit is not enforced at the time a part is uploaded, but is instead enforced at the time you attempt to  [complete the upload](/storage/docs/xml-api/post-object-complete). |
| Maximum length of time a [multipart upload](/storage/docs/multipart-uploads) and its uploaded parts can remain unfinished or idle in a bucket | Unlimited |  |
| Maximum number of different [multipart uploads](/storage/docs/multipart-uploads) that can simultaneously occur for an object | Unlimited |  |
| Maximum length of time to complete a [resumable upload session](/storage/docs/resumable-uploads) | 7 days | The length of time is measured starting from the resumable upload being initiated. |

## HMAC keys for service accounts

There is a limit of at most 10 [HMAC keys](/storage/docs/authentication/hmackeys) per service account. Deleted keys
don't count towards this limit.

## Inventory reports

There is a limit of at most 100 [inventory report configurations](/storage/docs/insights/inventory-reports#inventory-reports-overview) per source
bucket.

## Storage batch operations jobs

This section describes current API restrictions and usage quotas on use of
storage batch operations jobs.

### Concurrent storage batch operations jobs

The following table describes the limit for concurrent in-progress
[`jobs`](/storage/docs/storagebatchoperations/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.jobs):

| Maximum in-progress `jobs` | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| 100 | Per project per bucket's location |

### Rate quotas

Storage batch operations enforces rate quotas on all requests made.

This table provides the metric, API methods, and default limits for each quota:

| Metric | API methods | Default limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storagebatchoperations.googleapis.com/create_requests` | `storagebatchoperations.jobs.create` | 1200 requests/min/project |
| `storagebatchoperations.googleapis.com/read_requests` | * `storagebatchoperations.jobs.get` * `storagebatchoperations.jobs.list` | 1200 requests/min/project |
| `storagebatchoperations.googleapis.com/cancel_requests` | `storagebatchoperations.jobs.cancel` | 1200 requests/min/project |
| `storagebatchoperations.googleapis.com/delete_requests` | `storagebatchoperations.jobs.delete` | 1200 requests/min/project |

## Cloud Storage MCP server

This section describes limits and quotas for Cloud Storage MCP server. For instructions on how to use it, see [Use the Cloud Storage MCP server](/storage/docs/use-cloud-storage-mcp).

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum file size | 8 MiB |
| Supported endpoints | Global only |

The following table describes rate limits per tool:

| Quota | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Requests for `McpListBuckets`, `McpListObjects`, `McpReadText`, `McpGetObjectMetadata`, and `McpReadObject` | 600/min/project/region |
| Requests for `McpCreateBucket` and `McpWriteText` | 300/min/project/region |

## Bandwidth

| Quota | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum bandwidth for each [zone](/storage/docs/locations#location-z) that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services per project, per zone  Only available with [Rapid Bucket](/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-bucket). | 1 Tbps default quota per project, per zone, but might be lower or higher based on your project's billing account history | You can [request quota increases by using the Google Cloud console](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#increase) on a per-project, per-zone basis. Alternatively, you can request quota increases by contacting your Technical Account Manager or Google representative.  To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see [View and manage quotas](/docs/quotas/view-manage).  To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see [Bandwidth monitoring](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#bandwidth-monitoring).  For more information about zonal buckets, see [Rapid Bucket](/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-bucket). |
| Maximum bandwidth for each [region](/storage/docs/locations#location-r) that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services | 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history | Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN is exempt from this quota.  You can [request quota increases](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#increase) on a per-project basis.  To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see [View and manage quotas](/docs/quotas/view-manage).  To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see [Bandwidth monitoring](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#bandwidth-monitoring). |
| Maximum bandwidth for each [dual-region](/storage/docs/locations#location-dr) that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services | 200 Gbps default quota for each region within a dual-region for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history | Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN is exempt from this quota.  You can [request a quota increase](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#increase) on a per-project basis.  To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see [View and manage quotas](/docs/quotas/view-manage).  To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see [Bandwidth monitoring](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#bandwidth-monitoring). |
| Maximum bandwidth for each [multi-region](/storage/docs/locations#location-mr) that has data egress from Cloud Storage to Google services | 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history | Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN is exempt from this quota.  Each region within the given multi-region has a separate quota. For example, say the project `my-project` has a multi-region Google egress bandwidth quota of 200 Gbps for all regions within it. In this scenario, the `us-east1` region has 200 Gbps of bandwidth when supporting data egress to Google services from buckets in the `us` multi-region, and the `us-west1` region has 200 Gbps of bandwidth when supporting data egress to Google services from buckets in the `us` multi-region.  To learn how to view the Google egress limits for a project, see [View and manage quotas](/docs/quotas/view-manage).  To learn how to view Google egress usage for a project, see [Bandwidth monitoring](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#bandwidth-monitoring).  You can [request a quota increase](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#increase) on a per-project basis. Note that generally you should use buckets located in regions or dual-regions for workloads with high egress rates to Google services. For existing buckets in multi-regions that run large workloads in Google services, you can [use Storage Transfer Service to move your data](/storage/docs/moving-buckets) to a bucket in a region or dual-region. |
| Maximum egress bandwidth for Internet requests accessing data from buckets in a [region](/storage/docs/locations#location-r) | 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history | Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN due to [cache misses](/cdn/docs/overview#cache_hits_and_cache_misses) is included in this quota.  To learn how to view the Internet egress limits for a project, see [View and manage quotas](/docs/quotas/view-manage).  To learn how to view Internet egress usage for a project, see [Bandwidth monitoring](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#bandwidth-monitoring).  You can [request quota increases](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#increase) on a per-project basis. |
| Maximum egress bandwidth for Internet requests accessing data from buckets in a [dual-region](/storage/docs/locations#location-dr) | 200 Gbps default quota for each region within a dual-region for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history | Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN due to [cache misses](/cdn/docs/overview#cache_hits_and_cache_misses) is included in this quota.  To learn how to view the Internet egress limits for a project, see [View and manage quotas](/docs/quotas/view-manage).  To learn how to view Internet egress usage for a project by region, see [Bandwidth monitoring](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#bandwidth-monitoring).  You can [request a quota increase](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#increase) on a per-project basis. |
| Maximum egress bandwidth for Internet requests accessing data from buckets in a given [multi-region](/storage/docs/locations#location-mr) | 200 Gbps per region default quota for most projects, but might be lower based on your project's billing account history | Egress to Cloud CDN and Media CDN due to [cache misses](/cdn/docs/overview#cache_hits_and_cache_misses) is included in this quota.  Regions within the multi-region have separate multi-region Internet egress quotas. For example, say `my-project` sends data from a bucket located in the `us` multi-region to customers around the world. In this scenario, different regions within the `us` multi-region use their own Internet egress quota as data is sent from the bucket to different parts of the world. Typically, Internet egress quota is counted against the region that's geographically closest to the data's destination.  To learn how to view the Internet egress limits for a project, see [View and manage quotas](/docs/quotas/view-manage).  To learn how to view Internet egress usage for a project by region, see [Bandwidth monitoring](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#bandwidth-monitoring).  You can [request a quota increase](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage#increase) on a per-project basis. |

When a project's bandwidth exceeds a certain quota, requests to affected
buckets can be throttled or can be rejected with a [retryable](/storage/docs/retry-strategy)
`429 - rateLimitExceeded` error that includes details of the exceeded quota.
See [Bandwidth usage](/storage/docs/bandwidth-usage) for information about monitoring your bandwidth.
